prerequisites: Ability to read and understand documentation written in English.

learning_outcomes.text: Capacity for the direction of research, development and innovation projects in companies and technology centers, guaranteeing safety for people and property, the final quality of the products, and their homologation.
Know what R&D&I is, the functions an R&D&I manager must perform, and the methodologies to develop them.
Be able to prepare and direct R&D&I projects, ensuring their economic viability and the quality of their results.
Know the necessary mechanisms to protect R&D&I results.
Know how to design continuous evaluation and improvement plans for R&D&I.

syllabus_topics: T3 - Knowledge management and intellectual capital
T5 - R&D&I Management: methodologies and functions
P1 - Technology watch for a sector
P2 - Generation of ideas for innovation in a sector
P3 - Planning of an R&D&I Management System
P4 - Preparation of an R&D&I project
P5 - Financing of an R&D&I project

assessment_methods.method: Four written tests (T1, T2, T3, T4) for the theoretical block, including numerical problem solving.
Six group practical assignments (P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6) for the practical block.

assessment_rules: For continuous evaluation, a minimum grade of 5 out of 10 is required for both theoretical and practical blocks. Each theoretical test (T1-T4) and practical assignment (P1-P6) requires a minimum of 3 out of 10 to be compensable. Final continuous evaluation grade is calculated as 0.4 * Theoretical Block + 0.6 * Practical Block, provided minimums are met and attendance to practical classes is at least 85%. For ordinary, extraordinary, and differentiated calls, the same minimums apply, and previously approved blocks or parts are retained. If any block is not passed, the final grade will be the lowest grade of the failed block.
